extracted.intended_audience: ORR staff, care provider facilities, PRS providers, legal representatives, sponsors, and stakeholders involved in placement and post-release services for unaccompanied children
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed ORR regulatory standards and procedural requirements governing release, appeals, specific consent, post-release services (PRS), recordkeeping, notifications, and minimum standards for care provider facilities serving unaccompanied children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Denial in a language the child understands
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sole reason for denial of release is concern that the unaccompanied child is a danger to themself or the community, ORR must send the unaccompanied child a copy of the Notification of Denial letter in a language that the child understands (described at § 410.1205(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure translation/interpretation sufficient for the child's comprehension; this notification is required where denial is based solely on danger-to-self/others concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal right for parent or legal guardian potential sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: If the potential sponsor denied is the unaccompanied child's parent or legal guardian and is not already seeking appeal, the unaccompanied child may appeal the denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves strong parental interest; applies when parent/guardian is the denied sponsor and has not initiated appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to counsel for release or denial proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Unaccompanied children may have the assistance of counsel, at no cost to the Federal Government, with respect to release or the denial of release to a proposed sponsor (§ 410.1205(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR recognizes access to counsel for release decisions; counsel may assist in appeals or other release-related processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to submit appeal request (parents/legal guardians)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parents and legal guardians denied sponsorship may seek an appeal of ORR's decision by submitting a written request to the Assistant Secretary of ACF or the Assistant Secretary's neutral and detached designee (§ 410.1206(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals must be written and directed to the Assistant Secretary or designated neutral; establishes the formal filing channel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of appeal and acknowledgment timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals may be sought with or without a hearing and pursuant to processes described by ORR in agency guidance; the Assistant Secretary or designee will acknowledge the request for appeal within a reasonable time (§ 410.1206(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR will provide procedural options (hearing or not) and an acknowledgement; details and timing for hearings are set out in ORR guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child's right to appeal when danger-to-self/others is sole reason
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sole reason for denial is concern that the child poses a danger to self or others, the unaccompanied child may also appeal the release denial and may consult with their attorney or a legal service provider; they may seek such appeal any time after denial while in ORR custody (§ 410.1206(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special appeal pathway for children when safety concerns are the sole basis for denial; allows consultation with counsel and ongoing opportunity while in custody.

rubrics_metrics.name: 90‑Day Review of pending sponsor applications
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR federal staff supervising case management must review all pending sponsor applications or Family Reunification Packets (FRP) for children who have been in ORR custody 90 days after submission of the sponsor application or FRP to identify and resolve reasons for delay and determine steps to accelerate safe release (§ 410.1207(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures timely placement; review focuses on identifying and remedying outstanding obstacles preventing release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case status updates after 90‑day review
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of the review, UC Program case managers or designated staff must update the potential sponsor and child on case status and explain reasons the release process is incomplete (§ 410.1207(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency requirement—informing stakeholders of outstanding issues and planned actions to resolve them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic 90‑day follow-up reviews until resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: For cases not resolved after the initial 90‑Day Review, ORR federal staff supervising case management would conduct additional reviews at least every 90 days until the pending sponsor application or FRP is resolved (§ 410.1207(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates recurring monitoring to prioritize timeliness of placement until resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility categories for Unaccompanied Refugee Minors (URM) Program
rubrics_metrics.description: An unaccompanied child may be eligible for URM services including: (1) Cuban and Haitian entrants as defined by statute; (2) victims of a severe form of trafficking; (3) individuals determined to be Special Immigrant Juveniles under INA §101(a)(27)(J) who meet custody/service criteria; (4) individuals with U nonimmigrant status as authorized by TVPRA; (5) other populations authorized by Congress (§ 410.1208(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR lists statutory/immigration-status-based eligibility categories for URM referral; specific statutory references provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best interest evaluation for URM referral
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would evaluate each case to determine whether it is in the unaccompanied child's best interests to be referred to the URM Program (§ 410.1208(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral to URM is not automatic based solely on category; ORR conducts individualized best-interest determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal custody/guardianship requirement for URM placements
rubrics_metrics.description: When ORR discharges a child to receive services through the URM Program, the receiving entity must establish legal responsibility (custody or guardianship) under state law; until such custody is established, the ORR Director retains legal custody (§ 410.1208(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures legal responsibility transitions to receiving entity per state law; ORR retains custody until formal transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to request specific consent to invoke state juvenile court jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: An unaccompanied child in ORR custody is required to request specific consent from ORR if they seek to invoke a state juvenile court to determine or alter custody status or release from ORR custody (§ 410.1209(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific consent is a prerequisite when the child seeks state-court action that would change ORR custody or placement decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No specific consent required for SIJ‑predicate dependency orders
rubrics_metrics.description: If an unaccompanied child seeks a dependency order so they can petition for Special Immigrant Juvenile classification (SIJ predicate order), the child does not need HHS consent (§ 410.1209(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes requests to invoke state jurisdiction for SIJ predicate orders from other jurisdictional/placement-altering requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific consent request process and acknowledgement timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorneys or others acting on behalf of a child must complete a request for specific consent prior to a state juvenile court determining or altering custody; ORR would acknowledge receipt within two business days (§ 410.1209(c)–(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal submission requirements and prompt acknowledgement (2 business days) are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards ORR uses when adjudicating specific consent
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR will consider whether ORR custody is required to (1) ensure the child's safety or (2) ensure the safety of the community; ORR will not consider runaway risk for this purpose (§ 410.1209(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses the consent decision on safety to child/community rather than flight risk; aligns with statutory placement considerations (8 U.S.C. 1232(c)(2)(A)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframe for ORR decisions on specific consent requests
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall make determinations on specific consent requests within 60 business days of receipt and shall attempt to expedite urgent requests (§ 410.1209(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a 60-business-day decision target with an option to expedite urgent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice and evidence for specific consent decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall inform the child, the child's attorney, or authorized representative of the decision in writing, along with the evidence used to make the decision (§ 410.1209(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides transparency by disclosing the evidence base used in the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration procedure for denied specific consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The child, child's attorney, or EOIR accredited representative may request reconsideration with the Assistant Secretary for ACF within 30 business days of receipt of the notification of denial and may submit additional evidence (§ 410.1209(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a 30-business-day window to seek reconsideration and allows submission of new evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final administrative decision timeline on reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assistant Secretary for ACF or designee must consider the reconsideration request and any additional evidence and send a final administrative decision within 15 business days of receipt of the request (§ 410.1209(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a 15-business-day deadline for final administrative disposition after reconsideration submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and authorization for Post‑Release Services (PRS)
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS are provided by ORR-funded providers to facilitate access to relevant services during the pendency of removal proceedings for certain children and to promote safety and well-being after release; TVPRA authorizes or requires PRS in certain cases (§ 410.1210 introduction and (a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes legal basis and program purpose: facilitate safe transition and continuity of care post-release.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS provider role in release preparation and sponsor assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities and PRS providers must work with sponsors and children to prepare them for safe and timely release, assess sponsors' ability to access community resources, and provide guidance regarding safety planning and accessing services (§ 410.1210(a)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active role in pre-release planning and sponsor suitability/support capacity assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirement to provide PRS after home study; discretionary PRS for other needs
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR must conduct follow-up services during removal proceedings for children for whom a home study was conducted; ORR may provide PRS to children with mental health or other needs based on available appropriations (§ 410.1210(a)(2)–(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes mandated PRS (home-study cases per 8 U.S.C. 1232(c)(3)(B)) from discretionary PRS subject to funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive list of PRS service areas
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS should support access to services including placement and stability; immigration proceedings; guardianship; legal services; education; medical services; individual mental health services; family stabilization and counseling; substance use; gang prevention; education about employment laws/workers' rights; other specialized services; assistance in school enrollment and special education; family reunification and medical support; help obtaining medical records and documentation; and support accessing medical care (§ 410.1210(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR proposes to codify the ORR Guide's section 6.2.2 service areas; comprehensiveness depends on appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and reasonable modification obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS must be furnished in a manner sensitive to individual needs and in ways the child effectively understands regardless of language, reading comprehension, or disability; ORR and PRS entities must make reasonable modifications unless they would fundamentally alter the program (§ 410.1210(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures meaningful access for LEP and disabled children; allows ORR to decline fundamental alterations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health literacy requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers would be required to provide children and sponsors with information and services relevant to health-related considerations to increase awareness and ensure continuity of care after release (§ 410.1210(b)(7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports continuity of medical care and understanding of health needs post-release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority referrals for especially vulnerable children
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR proposes that children who are especially vulnerable (examples include those needing particular services/treatment; with disabilities; LGBTQI+ status; adjudicated delinquent or at risk of juvenile justice involvement; separated from parent/guardian by DHS; victims of human trafficking or other crimes; victims of worker exploitation; at risk for labor trafficking; chronically absent from school; certain parolees) may receive additional consideration and referral for PRS, including after release (§ 410.1210(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists illustrative vulnerable populations; referrals may occur based on post-release notifications or other reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment requirements for PRS providers
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers must assess the released child and sponsor for needed services and document the assessment; assessments must be developmentally appropriate, trauma‑informed (per proposed § 410.1001 and CDC/SAMHSA guidelines), and include validated trauma screening measures (§ 410.1210(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment must be tailored to cognitive/physical/emotional ability, trauma-informed, and use validated child-appropriate screening instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety and Well‑Being (SWB) calls practice (not codified)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR currently provides SWB follow-up calls to determine residence with sponsor, school enrollment/attendance, awareness of court dates, and safety; ORR plans to continue SWB calls but is not proposing to codify them in this rule and seeks public comment on codification and integration into PRS (§ 410.1210(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SWB calls are part of current practice; ORR is seeking comment on whether to codify or integrate them into PRS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation of PRS level in provider assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR is considering requiring PRS provider assessments to include a recommended level of PRS (based on regular and repeated assessments) that aligns the provider's engagement with child/sponsor needs; currently two levels exist (Level One and Level Two), and ORR is considering adding Level Three and codifying levels (§ 410.1210 discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should identify level(s) of service appropriate (safety check-ins, case management, intensive home engagement) and may recommend multiple levels as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions/examples of PRS levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Level One: needs assessment and assistance accessing community services (no intensive case management). Level Two: higher engagement including regularly scheduled home visits (at least once a month), ongoing needs assessments, comprehensive case management, and access to therapeutic support. ORR is considering Level Three to include intensive home engagements (§ 410.1210 discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR may require furnishing specific levels for children mandated to receive PRS; descriptions give examples of service intensity and activities per level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframes and reassessment for PRS levels
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR is considering minimum time limits for PRS levels (at least six months after release) and reassessment intervals (e.g., assess every 30 days after Level Three); PRS may continue beyond minimum timeframes where needed but not past termination circumstances (§ 410.1210 discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides possible baseline duration and periodic reassessment cadence to determine ongoing need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule and minimum contact frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS provider, in consultation with the child and sponsor, decides methods, timeframes, and schedule; proposed minimum is monthly contact (in person or virtual) for six months after release (§ 410.1210(e)(1)–(2)). ORR is considering limiting minimum monthly contact to Level Two/Three recipients and seeks comment on factors determining contact frequency (§ 410.1210(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers must at least attempt monthly contact for six months (subject to ORR's final decision) and document contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of contacts, home visits, progress and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers would be required to document all ongoing check-ins and in-home visits as well as the progress and outcomes of those home visits (§ 410.1210(e)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed documentation supports monitoring and outcomes assessment; documentation must be uploaded per recordkeeping rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance accessing community resources
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers must work with released children and sponsors to ensure access to community resources; examples include helping make appointments, request interpretation services, understand service costs, enroll in school/childcare/preschool, and connect to legal services, education/ESL, youth programming, medical and behavioral healthcare, cultural services, and supports for independence and integration (§ 410.1210(f)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR intentionally does not enumerate all methods—assistance may vary by case; examples illustrate expected scope of help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of referrals and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers are required to document any community resource referrals and their outcomes (§ 410.1210(f)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must capture referral activity and whether referrals resulted in successful connections or services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframes to start PRS after release or referral
rubrics_metrics.description: For children required to receive PRS, providers must, to the greatest extent practicable, start services within two days of release and no later than 30 days; for children referred but not mandated by home study, providers must, to the greatest extent practicable, start services within two days of accepting a referral (§ 410.1210(g)(1)–(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes rapid initiation of services to ensure continuity; 'to the greatest extent practicable' language acknowledges operational constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination criteria for mandated PRS
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS mandated pursuant to TVPRA continue until the child turns 18, or the child is granted voluntary departure, immigration status, or receives an order of removal; if voluntary departure or removal occurs, PRS is discontinued until repatriation and ends when the child's case is closed (§ 410.1210(h)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines statutory end points for mandated follow-up services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination criteria for non‑mandated PRS
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS for children not mandated by home study continue for not less than six months or until the child turns 18, whichever occurs first; PRS may end earlier if provider assesses services are no longer needed but must still be furnished for at least six months (§ 410.1210(h)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a minimum duration for discretionary PRS while allowing case-by-case clinical assessment to terminate services after the minimum period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive, confidential, and current case file maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers must maintain comprehensive, accurate, and current case files that are kept confidential and secure and accessible to ORR upon request; all case file information must be kept together in physical and electronic files (§ 410.1210(i)(1)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes file completeness, confidentiality, and ORR access for oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely upload of service documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers must upload all documentation related to services provided to children and sponsors to ORR's case management system, as available, within seven days of completion of the services (§ 410.1210(i)(1)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a seven-day upload deadline to keep ORR records timely and current.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and physical controls over records
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to providing PRS, providers must establish written policies/procedures for organizing and maintaining active and closed case files and administrative/physical controls to prevent unauthorized access (e.g., keeping sensitive health information locked when not in use) (§ 410.1210(i)(2)(i)–(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers must implement concrete record-protection measures and document policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on sharing records and transfers upon contract end
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collected should not be shared for other purposes except coordinating services; PRS providers may not release records to any third party without prior ORR approval. If the provider is no longer providing PRS, they must provide all active and closed case file records in original format to ORR per ORR's instructions (§ 410.1210(i)(2)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects confidentiality and controls dissemination; requires transfer of records back to ORR upon termination of provider involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and encryption requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers must have written policies and procedures protecting sensitive information from unauthorized access, including encrypting electronic communications containing sensitive healthcare or identifying information; they must explain to children and sponsors how/when sensitive information may be shared and have appropriate internal controls on information sharing (§ 410.1210(i)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit requirement to use encryption and to communicate privacy practices to families and children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Concern (NOC) procedures and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: If a PRS provider is concerned about a child's safety and well‑being, it must notify ORR and appropriate agencies (e.g., law enforcement, child protective services) and submit a NOC; examples of triggers are listed (emergency, trafficking, abuse/neglect, exploitative employment, kidnapping/runaway, alleged criminal activity, lost contact for 30 days, etc.). Providers must submit a NOC within 24 hours of first knowledge or suspicion and document it (§ 410.1210(i)(4)(i)–(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies both the substantive triggers for reporting and a strict 24‑hour reporting requirement for suspected safety concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case closure procedures and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: A case file must be formally closed when PRS are terminated by ORR; ORR will supply instructions and relevant forms that providers must follow; ORR may require providers to complete a case closure form and upload it to ORR's system within 72 hours of case closure (§ 410.1210(i)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes formal closure process and a 72‑hour upload expectation for closure documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Subpart D: minimum standards and required services
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure all unaccompanied children receive the same minimum services and a specified level of quality, ORR proposes minimum standards and required services consistent with statutory authorities and principles of treating children with dignity, respect, and special concern for vulnerability (§ 410.1300).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames Subpart D as codifying baseline quality standards across placement settings; ORR invites public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of minimum standards tailored to placement setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities serving unaccompanied children should meet standards tailored to their particular placement setting so children receive at least the same standard of care within a given placement setting (§ 410.1301).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards are to be setting-specific (e.g., foster care, group care) to ensure consistency of care quality within each placement type.
